title: Castillos et al. 2023, m-sequence c-VEP, 40% amplitude depth: Burst c-VEP Based BCI: Optimizing stimulus design for enhanced classification with minimal calibration data and improved user experience
description: EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing an offline 4-class reactive BCI task based on code-modulated visual evoked potentials (c-VEP). This subset contains the m-sequence condition at 40% amplitude depth, from a factorial study comparing burst and m-sequence codes at 100% and 40% modulation depth. The data support evaluation of CNN-based classification with minimal calibration data and the visual comfort of reduced-intensity stimuli.
methods_description: 32-channel EEG was recorded with a BrainProducts LiveAmp at 500 Hz (impedance below 25 kOhm). Participants attended to four cued disc targets flickering on a 60 Hz monitor; each trial had a 0.5 s cue, 2.2 s stimulation and 0.7 s inter-trial interval, with 15 blocks of 4 trials per condition. Preprocessing included average re-referencing, a 49.9-50.1 Hz IIR notch filter, epoching and baseline removal. Classification used a CNN with sliding windows for bitwise decoding.
